properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 is used for hashing in server/etcdserver/api/membership/cluster.go and server/etcdserver/api/membership/member.go. This is a known vulnerability as SHA-1 is collision-broken.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: JWT RS256/PS256 signatures are used for authentication. These use RSA signatures which are vulnerable to Shor's algorithm and need migration to ML-DSA.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RSA is used for JWT signing in authentication components. This is a classical cryptography vulnerability that would be susceptible to Shor's algorithm.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: JWT HS256 signatures are used for authentication. While HMAC-SHA256 is not directly vulnerable to Shor's algorithm, the JWT system using it still represents a security concern in the overall authentication architecture.

components.name: Go crypto/tls sessions on default settings (Go 1.27)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA signatures are used for authentication and certificate validation. While ECDSA is not directly broken by Shor's algorithm like RSA, it is still part of the classical cryptographic landscape that needs to be considered for post-quantum migration.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 signatures are used for authentication in JWT tokens. While Ed25519 is considered quantum-safe, the overall architecture using it needs to be reviewed as part of a comprehensive security posture.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TLS 1.2 is being used for secure communication. While TLS 1.2 itself isn't broken by Shor's algorithm, it uses classical cryptography (RSA/ECDH) that will be vulnerable to quantum attacks and needs migration to TLS 1.3 with post-quantum key exchange.

properties.name: pqs:context
